name: IceCube-Gen2
summary: Proposed major successor expansion of IceCube, covering high-energy neutrino and multimessenger astronomy and extending new-physics tests including heavy dark-matter decay.
detection_principle: A larger optical ice-Cherenkov array combined with high-energy radio-detection concepts; deep ice is the interaction medium.

sites.name: Ice surrounding IceCube at the South Pole, planned
sites.location: Ice surrounding IceCube at the South Pole, planned

status.label: Proposal
status.evidence: The design announcement describes a future expansion, distinct from the IceCube Upgrade currently being deployed.

key_parameters.name: Optical volume
key_parameters.value: About 8 km³, a 2020 design target rather than a constructed value

phases.name: Complete Gen2 array
phases.description: Separate from the smaller upgrade of existing IceCube

science_scope: Tests dark-matter models through astrophysical radiation, cosmic rays or neutrinos. Astrophysical backgrounds and propagation models affect interpretation; an anomaly alone does not establish dark matter.
